headline: Iranian spies buried command traffic in Microsoft 365 calendars, attackers began exploiting a critical ServiceNow pre-authentication flaw, and the FakeGit campaign flooded GitHub with 7,600 malware repositories.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep dressing malware as artificial-intelligence tooling, and the FakeGit campaign cloned nearly 7,600 GitHub repositories—more than 800 posing as AI skills or Model Context Protocol servers—to push SmartLoader onto developers.
emerging_trends.topic_title: FakeGit and SleeperGem Flood Open-Source Registries

emerging_trends.text: Espionage crews increasingly route command traffic through trusted cloud services, and HollowGraph now buries operator instructions and stolen files inside Microsoft 365 calendar events dated to the year 2050.
emerging_trends.topic_title: HollowGraph Hides C2 in Microsoft 365 Calendars

emerging_trends.text: Critical enterprise flaws move from disclosure to mass exploitation within days, as attackers hit the ServiceNow AI Platform and the freshly disclosed WordPress WP2Shell bugs almost as soon as details went public.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Actively Exploited ServiceNow AI Platform RCE

topics.title: Fresh Breaches Hit Consumers, Telecom, and Governments
topics.latest_developments: Microtask platform Paidwork exposed data on more than 23 million users; Italy's Garante per la Protezione dei Dati Personali fined WINDTRE €1.7 million over two February 2025 breaches affecting more than 365,000 customers; hackers lurked nine months inside South Korea's diplomatic academy training system, stealing Ministry of Foreign Affairs staff data; and Romania's land registry agency is still recovering from what it called its most serious technical incident.
topics.summary: The day's breaches span a gig-work platform, an Italian telecom, a South Korean government training system, and a Romanian property registry, with old-school social engineering behind the WINDTRE intrusions; affected users should watch for phishing and fraud tied to exposed personal data.

sources.title: Paidwork breach exposes sensitive data of 23 million user
Italy fines WINDTRE €1.7 million over security flaws behind two data breaches
Hackers were inside South Korea's diplomat training system for 9 months
Romania races to restore land registry after cyberattack disrupts property market

topics.title: HollowGraph Hides C2 in Microsoft 365 Calendars
topics.latest_developments: Group-IB named HollowGraph, an espionage implant that hijacks a compromised Microsoft 365 calendar as its command channel, planting tasking and exfiltrating stolen files as attachments on events dated to 2050 so the activity blends into legitimate Microsoft Graph traffic.
topics.summary: Group-IB ties HollowGraph with high confidence to the modular Cavern backdoor framework and Iranian espionage; because commands and data move through normal Graph API calls, defenders should hunt for anomalous calendar events and far-future appointment dates in Microsoft 365 mailboxes.

sources.title: New HollowGraph malware uses Microsoft Graph for stealthy C2 comms
HOLLOWGRAPH malware turns Microsoft 365 calendars into an espionage channel
HollowGraph Malware Hides C2 and Stolen Files in Microsoft 365 Events Dated 2050

topics.title: Actively Exploited ServiceNow AI Platform RCE
topics.latest_developments: Threat-intelligence firm Defused reported that attackers began exploiting CVE-2026-6875, a critical pre-authentication code-injection flaw in the ServiceNow AI Platform.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-6875 lets an unauthenticated attacker escape ServiceNow's script sandbox and run code remotely on a targeted instance; every organization running the AI Platform-as-a-Service should patch immediately.

sources.title: ServiceNow pre-auth RCE exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-6875)
Critical ServiceNow code execution flaw now exploited in attacks

topics.title: FakeGit and SleeperGem Flood Open-Source Registries
topics.latest_developments: Researchers exposed FakeGit, nearly 7,600 malicious GitHub repositories—more than 800 impersonating AI skills or Model Context Protocol servers—that deliver the SmartLoader malware, while a separate campaign called SleeperGem published three malicious RubyGems, including git_credential_manager and Dendreo, to serve follow-on payloads to developer machines.
topics.summary: Both campaigns weaponize the trust developers place in package registries, using copied projects, lookalike profiles, and convincing READMEs to smuggle loaders and stealers; teams should vet dependencies and repository provenance before installing.

sources.title: FakeGit Campaign Uses 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread SmartLoader Malware
SleeperGem Uses Three Malicious RubyGems Packages to Target Developer Machines

topics.title: Ransomware Payment Bans and World Leaks Extortion
topics.latest_developments: Ars Technica reported that a ransomware surge is pushing governments to weigh outright bans on ransom payments, as Indian officials confirmed the World Leaks group claimed files from the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant but said the documents hold no safety or security information.
topics.summary: Rising ransomware sophistication has victims facing pay-or-refuse dilemmas while regulators consider prohibiting payments; World Leaks' Kudankulam claim shows extortion crews targeting critical infrastructure even when the stolen files prove less sensitive than advertised.

sources.title: Pay up or not? Ransomware surge has victims facing tough choices.
India says allegedly leaked nuclear plant files pose no safety risk

topics.title: Apps for US Troops Ship Chinese and Russian Code
topics.latest_developments: A first-of-its-kind Wired analysis found that more than one in eight apps built for US service members carry foreign code, some of it from firms in nations the Pentagon designates as adversaries.
topics.summary: The study exposes a supply-chain risk in software marketed to military users, where embedded Chinese and Russian components could hand adversaries access to sensitive personnel; the Pentagon and app vendors face pressure to audit code provenance.

sources.title: Apps Marketed to US Troops Are Shipping Chinese and Russian Code

business_politics.title: Iran War Pushes Gas Past $4 as Mediators Seek Truce
business_politics.latest_developments: Gas topped $4 a gallon nationally for the first time in a month, Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthis threatened to blockade Saudi crude exports through the Red Sea, and regional mediators narrowed talks toward a proposed 10-day ceasefire.
business_politics.summary: U.S. and Iranian forces have fought openly since early July; Iran struck Gulf tankers Monday to briefly lift Brent crude near $90 a barrel, the U.S. average pump price crossed $4.003 as strikes hit Middle East oil infrastructure, and a wider spiral now threatens Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export route.

business.title: Gas Tops $4 a Gallon Again
business.latest_developments: AAA data showed the national gas average hit $4.003 Monday, the first crossing above $4 in over a month, as U.S.-Iran fighting drove up oil.
business.summary: The U.S. average gasoline price crossed $4 a gallon for the first time in over a month, pushed by escalating U.S.-Iran strikes on Middle East oil infrastructure; rising diesel threatens to lift the cost of groceries and other goods trucked into Pittsburgh.

business.title: Judge Halts Paramount-Warner Merger
business.latest_developments: A federal judge issued a 14-day restraining order Monday blocking Paramount Skydance's takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, with a hearing set for August 3, after a coalition of states sued.
business.summary: California district judge granted the states a temporary halt to the roughly $81 billion Paramount Skydance–Warner Bros. Discovery deal, citing compelling evidence the combined firm would hold substantial share of the wide-release theatrical distribution market.

sources.title: Judge temporarily halts Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger

around_town.summary: PennDOT's replacement of the Commercial Street Bridge on the Parkway East (I-376) reached a milestone as contractors moved the new span into place; an early reopening would end weeks of closures on the busy corridor east of Downtown Pittsburgh.
